title: Header Trust & Proxy Attacks
description: Trust-boundary errors in reverse proxy headers and origin routing.

attacks.name: X-Forwarded-For trust
attacks.notes: Spoof IP → bypass rate limit/IP allowlist
attacks.desc: Trusting a client-supplied forwarding address can bypass IP-based rate limits or allowlists.
attacks.prevention: Accept client IP headers only from known reverse proxies, and derive security decisions from a trusted proxy chain.

attacks.name: X-Forwarded-Host trust
attacks.desc: A trusted forwarded-host value can poison generated links, including password-reset URLs.
attacks.prevention: Generate password-reset URLs from a configured canonical origin, not from untrusted forwarded-host values.

attacks.name: X-Original-URL / X-Rewrite-URL
attacks.desc: Rewrite headers can make a proxy authorize one path while the backend serves another.
attacks.prevention: Strip untrusted rewrite headers at the edge and authorize the final backend route.

attacks.name: X-Forwarded-Proto
attacks.desc: A spoofed forwarded-protocol value can change URL generation, redirects, or secure-cookie decisions.
attacks.prevention: Trust X-Forwarded-Proto only from configured proxies and enforce HTTPS decisions from verified connection data.

attacks.name: Host header variations
attacks.desc: Ambiguous Host values can make routing, security checks, and generated links disagree on the intended authority.

attacks.name: Absolute-URI request line
attacks.desc: An absolute URI in the request line may be routed or validated differently from an origin-form path.

attacks.name: Hop-by-hop header abuse
attacks.desc: A Connection header can nominate other headers as hop-by-hop, causing a proxy to strip data the backend expects.

attacks.name: Duplicate Host headers
attacks.desc: Two Host headers can be interpreted differently by separate HTTP components, affecting routing or authorization.

attacks.name: Origin IP discovery
attacks.desc: Historical DNS and host indexes may reveal a CDN-protected origin address.

attacks.name: Session persistence LB
attacks.notes: Sticky cookie → pin to old version
attacks.desc: Sticky routing can keep a session on an older backend with different security controls.

attacks.name: WAF bypass encoding
attacks.desc: Alternate encodings can evade a WAF when the protected application decodes input differently.
